results.title: NVIDIA continues to be a workhorse for us and the industry as a whole well into 2027. Really nice post here by Bill Hsu on the compute price curve. | Mike Canevaro
highlights:
**Reshared from Bill Hsu:**
> Kalshi is Building First Compute Forward Curve
>
> After NVDA's $500bn plan to mobilize PE capital for AI infra, the financialization of compute should accelerate.
>
> Apollo Global Management, Inc., BlackRock and KKR need to answer a basic question:
>
> Six or twelve months from now, how much will an hour of compute from these GPUs actually be worth?
>
> Kalshi is trying to answer that question for the private equity financing the buildout.
>
> Between September 2026 and March 2027, the market prices imply very different paths across four NVIDIA GPU generations.
>
> - B200 falls from $5.83 to $5.30 per GPU hour, down 9%.
> - H200 falls from $4.61 to $4.27, down 7%.
> - H100 rises from $2.62 to $2.77, up 6%.
> - A100 stays roughly flat, moving from $1.10 to $1.12.
>
> B200 and H200 still carry scarcity premiums. Their downward curves suggest that traders expect new capacity to come online and supply to catch up.
>
> H100 and A100 look closer to an economic floor. They are older and cheaper, but may still have stable demand from inference and more price sensitive workloads. There is simply less scarcity premium left to compress.
>
> That difference matters for financing.
>
> A lender should not apply the same depreciation assumption to every GPU. A B200 may be more valuable today, but its rental income could decline faster as supply expands. An H100 may generate less revenue, but its cash flow could prove more stable.
>
> Prediction markets are already aggregating views on GPU supply, customer demand, capacity expansion, and technological obsolescence into a visible price signal.
>
> The market is still early. Liquidity is thin, most participants are probably speculators, and the benchmark may not match the rental price of a specific cluster, region, or SLA.
>
> But if NVIDIA’s financing push turns compute into a major credit asset class, these signals could eventually influence GPU residual values, loan to value assumptions, insurance pricing, and hedge design.
>
> Capital is arriving. Prediction markets are beginning to tell us what the underlying compute might be worth.

results.title: Your GPU Reservation Expires This Quarter. Now What? | GPUaaS.com
highlights:
GPUaaS.com Team GPU Infrastructure August 19, 2026

Reserved H100 rates run from $1.07 to $10.14 per hour. Median $5.52.

Split by channel: marketplace median $1.70, neocloud median $2.31, hyperscaler median $6.11. The hyperscaler median is 3.3 times the combined non-hyperscaler median for identical silicon.

Key takeaways

- Prices fell 64-75% from peak, but expiring contracts have not softened the market. Several neoclouds announced 20% increases, and on-demand is effectively sold out
- Renewal leverage comes from holding hard-to-replace capacity, not from the price decline. Those are different negotiations
- Three clauses matter more than the rate: step-downs at 12 and 24 months, SKU flexibility across a generation, and a defined 10-20% burst allowance
- Under ASC 842, leases under 12 months can be operating leases. Longer terms generally capitalize as right-of-use assets, which finance may care about more than the rate
- Competitive bidding cuts 15-20% on comparable deals. Most teams renew against a single quote because the incumbent relationship feels easier

◆ RESERVED H100 PRICING BY CHANNEL

| Channel | Median reserved rate | Against combined non-hyperscaler median |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Marketplace | $1.70/hr | Below |
| Neocloud | $2.31/hr | Near |
| Hyperscaler | $6.11/hr | Roughly 3.3x |
| All channels combined | $5.52/hr median, $1.07-$10.14 range | Reference |

Source: Compute Exchange reserved GPU pricing data, 2026

...

Prices fell. The market did not loosen.

A team renewing inside a hyperscaler agreement without checking the other two channels is renewing against the most expensive third of the market.

H100 rental prices have fallen 64 to 75% from their 2023 peak. Expiring A100 and H100 contracts are flowing back into availability channels now. Pricing has not softened in response. Several neocloud providers have announced 20% increases. On-demand capacity across most GPU types is effectively sold out, and providers are renewing existing contracts rather than releasing capacity to the open market.

The leverage at renewal is real. It runs the opposite direction from what the price decline suggests. The position is not "prices collapsed, match the new rate." The position is holding capacity that is hard to replace on short notice.

◆ VERIFY BEFORE THE NOTICE WINDOW CLOSES

Lapsing on an assumption is the expensive mistake

Letting a reservation lapse on the assumption that on-demand will absorb the workload is the expensive mistake at this point in the cycle. The gap between capacity commitment and volume production runs 18 to 24 months. Current constraints persist into 2027. Verify on-demand availability for the specific tier and region before the notice window closes, not after.

...

Obsolescence risk on a short H100 renewal is lower than it looks. B200 capacity is allocated through the second half of 2027. Major cloud providers now assume a five to six year useful life for GPU infrastructure. A one or two year H100 commitment signed now carries relatively little risk of the hardware becoming unrentable inside the term. The risk sits in three-year and longer commitments, where H100 systems face roughly 40% value decline once the next generation ships in volume.

highlights: Nebius just cleared a major hurdle for its Vineland, New Jersey data center and its recent earnings back up why that matters so much (Save this). Nebius is building a hyperscale AI data center in Vineland, developed alongside construction partner DataOne, specifically to supply GPU capacity under a five year, $17.4 billion contract with Microsoft that can expand to $19.4 billion if Microsoft's usage scales up. The site sits on roughly 106 acres on South Lincoln Avenue, a former sand mining related industrial property and the full campus is designed to reach about 2.6 million square feet with somewhere between 300 and 350 megawatts of capacity once complete. To put that in perspective, 300 megawatts is described locally as nearly double the entire city of Vineland's current power usage, which is why the project has drawn real scrutiny from residents over water and electricity demands. Phase one is already under construction and reportedly finished an initial buildout in just twenty weeks, while Phase two, covering expansion plus major power, cooling, LNG, and water infrastructure using Bloom Energy fuel cells, just received Planning Board site plan approval yesterday night. That approval vote passed 9 to 1, clearing construction to continue and formally locking in the 300 megawatts of capacity at the site. Nebius guided for 800 megawatts to 1 gigawatt of total connected power by the end of 2026 and Vineland's 300 megawatts alone represents roughly 30% of that entire full year target, so getting this single site cleared removes a major chunk of execution risk from hitting guidance. Some stop work issues remain on specific unpermitted elements that still need proper permits before that portion of work can fully resume and full operations at the site are projected for 2027 but the core approval is now secured. That de-risking lands right on top of a blowout Q2 2026 print, with revenue hitting $582 million, up 454% year over year and up 46% sequentially, easily beating the Street's roughly $570 million estimate. Management reaffirmed full year guidance of $7-9 billion in annualized run rate revenue and $20-25 billion in capex and notably raised its contracted power target to 5 GW as customers help fund more of the buildout, which is exactly the kind of demand signal that makes locking down sites like Vineland so urgent. That surging demand shows up clearly in the broader GPU rental market too, where non hyperscaler cloud providers have seen prices climb sharply across nearly every chip this year, with H200 rental rates up to $3.28 per GPU hour and B200 rates near $5.61 per GPU hour as of August 2026, both well off their late-2025 lows. Even older H100 chips are commanding roughly $2.74 per GPU hour, up from around $2.00 late last year, showing that the capacity crunch driving Nebius's premium pricing is a market wide phenomenon. On the call, management also revealed it just signed its first short term capacity deal, a new type of contract lasting three to six months built for customers with an acute, time bound need for compute, such as a time boxed large scale training run ahead of a model release or a reinforcement learning post training sprint. These short duration deals command a significant premium, with management negotiating pricing in the $40-50 million per megawatt range and sometimes higher, well above the $20-25 million per megawatt typical of standard one to three year contracts, and the capacity for this first short-term deal is expected to go live in the fourth quarter. results.title: Ornn Wants Wall Street to Trade AI Compute Prices Like Oil - Startup Fortune
highlights:
Ornn is the startup trying to supply that number. Founded in 2025 by Kush Bavaria and Wayne Nelms, who a16z crypto says met at MIT, the New York company publishes the Ornn Compute Price Index, a transaction-based benchmark for GPU rental prices. Its own April announcement said the index had been added to the Bloomberg Terminal and was already being used by more than 400 data center operators, investors and AI companies.

The Blackwell price spike is the hook. Several outlets citing Ornn's index reported that renting an advanced Nvidia Blackwell GPU rose to $4.08 an hour in April, up 48% from $2.75 two months earlier. That isn't gentle movement for infrastructure sold as on-demand capacity. If you're an AI company running agents that call tools, retry tasks and burn through tokens all day, that price is not an abstraction. It lands in your monthly bill.

## The Price Wall Street Wants

Intercontinental Exchange announced on May 19 that it planned to launch U.S. dollar, cash-settled GPU compute futures tied to Ornn's Compute Price Index, pending regulatory approval. The contracts are meant to settle against live-traded spot prices for GPU compute across major hardware types, not a cloud provider's posted rate card.

CME Group has now moved too. On August 11, it said it would launch Silicon Data H100 Rental Index Futures and Silicon Data B200 Rental Index Futures on October 5, 2026, also pending regulatory review. Each contract will represent a month's worth of rent for the relevant Nvidia GPU, using hourly rental-rate indexes published by Silicon Data.

That is the real signal here. ICE, CME and Kalshi are not all circling compute because the phrase sounds fashionable.

...

Neoclouds such as CoreWeave and Nebius sit near the middle of that map. They buy large blocks of Nvidia capacity and lock in long contracts - then rent that access back to AI labs and enterprise customers. Investors have rewarded that exposure, then punished it whenever the financing starts to look too heavy. MarketWatch reported Wednesday that Nebius fell after announcing a $4.5 billion convertible bond offering, while Investor's Business Daily noted that CoreWeave carries more than $46 billion in debt against about $5 billion in equity.

results.title: NVIDIA H200 Compute Price Forecast: 2026 Prediction Market Analysis
highlights:
- Prediction Market Disconnect: Robinhood contracts price a 79% likelihood that NVIDIA H200 compute rates exceed $5.79/hr before December 31, 2026, despite spot rates softening from $5.11/hr in mid-August to $4.51/hr on September 1.
- The "Middle-Generation Squeeze": Empirical data from Ornn Data's September 2026 whitepaper reveals that H200 is the least cost-efficient GPU for sparse MoE models (`gpt-oss-120b` compute cost is $0.98/M tokens on H200 vs. $0.29 on A100 and $0.47 on B200).
- Steepest Forward Term Decay: Ornn's forward curve marks show H200 suffering the steepest pricing decay of any datacenter family: retaining only 51.0% of its one-month price at 3 years and 43.7% at 5 years (implied forward for years 4–5 drops to 33%).
- Memory Moat vs. Throughput Economics: While 141GB HBM3e provides high bandwidth (4.8 TB/s) for extreme single-device context, throughput-per-dollar economics for open-weight agentic workloads strongly favor either lower-cost A100/H100 or dense B200 clusters.
- Infrastructure Buffers: Regional grid interconnection delays and Rubin platform validation delays prevent immediate fleet retirement, but cannot fully offset Blackwell supply pressure.
- Revised Peak Forecast Band: Recalibrated modeling projects fourth-quarter 2026 peak spot rates between $4.65 and $5.45/hr, suggesting Robinhood contracts above $5.79 are significantly overpriced.

Robinhood prediction markets show strong confidence that NVIDIA H200 compute rental prices will rise before December 31, 2026. Event contracts price the probability of hourly rates exceeding $5.79 at 79%, exceeding $6.09 at 75%, and exceeding $6.39 at 70%. However, empirical data from Ornn Data’s September 2026 market report indicates that the underlying Ornn index tracked H200 spot instances at $4.51 per hour on September 1, 2026 / Ornn/ / Ornn Data/, pulling back from mid-August highs near $5.11. To breach the lower strike of $5.79 before year-end expiration, H200 rates must appreciate by over 28.4%—a steep climb given emerging competitive pressures across the hardware fleet.

...

When evaluating token-generation cost on sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) models such as `gpt-oss-120b` (117B total, 5.1B active parameters), the hardware cost hierarchy reverses completely:

- A100 SXM4 (80GB):$0.29 per million output tokens (at base utilization u = 0.5, h = 0.15)
- B200:$0.47 per million output tokens
- H100 SXM:$0.64 per million output tokens
- H200 SXM:$0.98 per million output tokens

Because sparse MoE architectures execute only a fraction of their parameters per token, memory bandwidth requirements are relaxed relative to parameter footprint. On single-device GPUStack runs, an A100 delivers 2,276 tok/s against H200’s 3,013 tok/s on MLPerf v6.0—a modest 32% performance delta that fails to justify H200’s 350% higher rental price ($4.51 vs $1.00/hr). For high-throughput server production, B200’s massive 8,949 server tok/s makes it far cheaper per token ($0.47) than H200 ($0.98). Consequently, price-sensitive open-weight workloads—such as agentic rollouts and reinforcement learning sandboxes at providers like Modal Labs / Modal Labs/—route around H200 in favor of either cheap A100/H100 instances or ultra-dense B200 clusters.

highlights:
5 Ekim'de GPU Kira Bedeline Endeksli Vadeli İşlem Geliyor - TokenPost

# 5 Ekim'de GPU Kira Bedeline Endeksli Vadeli İşlem Geliyor

 19 Ağustos Çarşamba, 2026 20:51 

GPU kartları ve vadeli işlem sözleşmesi belgelerinin bulunduğu bir toplantı masası / TokenPost.ai

Yapay zeka modellerinin eğitiminde ve işletilmesinde kullanılan GPU kira bedelleri, vadeli işlem sözleşmelerinin dayanak varlığı haline geliyor. Veri merkezi ve çip yatırımlarının büyümesiyle birlikte, compute maliyetini fiyatlandırma ve dalgalanma riskini yönetme talebi finans piyasalarına taşınıyor.

CME Group ve Silicon Data, H100 kira endeksi vadeli işlemleri ile B200 kira endeksi vadeli işlemlerini 2026'nın 5 Ekim'inde piyasaya süreceklerini 11'inde (yerel saatle) duyurdu. İki ürün de düzenleyici incelemeye tabi olacak ve sırasıyla Nvidia(NVDA) H100 ile Blackwell B200 GPU'larının bir aylık kiralama maliyetini yansıtacak.

TechCrunch'a göre Silicon Data, yakın zamanda tamamladığı Seri A turunda 30 milyon dolar topladı. Şirket, GPU kiralama fiyatları için bir referans endeksi ve Wall Street'teki vadeli işlem sözleşmelerinin takas standardını oluşturmayı hedefliyor.

Turu Valor Atreides AI Fonu yönetti. CME Group, DRW, Samsung, VanEck, Jump ve Wintermute de yatırımcılar arasında yer aldı.

Ürünün özü, fiziki GPU alım satımı değil. H100, A100 ve B200 gibi GPU'ların kira fiyatlarını standart bir 'endeks'te toplayıp, bu endeksi vadeli işlem sözleşmesinin referans fiyatı olarak kullanmak asıl amaç.

Silicon Data, GPU kira fiyat endeksini her iş gününde hesaplıyor. Şirketin açıkladığı 3 Ağustos verilerine göre H100 neocloud kira endeksi saatte 2,78 dolar, hyperscaler endeksi ise saatte 7,18 dolar seviyesindeydi. B200 kira endeksi ise saatte 5,65 dolar olarak açıklandı.

Compute, yapay zeka modellerini eğitmek ya da hizmet olarak sunmak için gereken işlem gücünü ifade ediyor. Bugüne kadar GPU kira bedelleri; tedarikçiye, bölgeye, sözleşme süresine ve müşteri büyüklüğüne göre değişiyordu. Bu yüzden aynı çip kullanılsa bile şirketlerin fiilen ödediği maliyeti karşılaştırmak zordu.

Vadeli işlem, gelecekte belirli bir tarihte önceden belirlenmiş bir fiyattan dayanak varlığın alınıp satılmasını taahhüt eden bir türev üründür. Bu ürünlerde fiziki GPU teslimatı değil, endeks üzerinden nakdi uzlaşma yapılacak. Amaç, yapay zeka geliştiricilerinin ve bulut sağlayıcılarının maliyet dalgalanması riskini ayrı bir araçla yönetebilmesi.

...

Carmen Li(Carmen Li) Silicon Data CEO'su ise "Aynı GPU kapasitesini satın alan iki şirket birbirinden tamamen farklı fiyatlar ödese bile, hangisinin daha iyi bir anlaşma yaptığını anlamanın bir yolu yoktu" dedi. Şirketlere göre kamuya açık bir referans fiyatın oluşması, GPU tedarik maliyetlerinin karşılaştırılma biçimini ve bütçe planlamasını değiştirebilir.

Piyasa yapısı gereği GPU kira fiyatları tek bir fiyata yakınsamakta zorlanıyor. Büyük bulut sözleşmeleri, neocloud işletmecileri ve kısa vadeli kiralama talebi birbirinden farklı koşullarda hareket ediyor. Endeksleme girişimi, bu dağınık fiyatları tek bir işlem görebilir referansta birleştirmeyi amaçlıyor.

...

Compute vadeli işlemlerinin fiilen işlem görebilmesi için düzenleyici incelemeden geçmesi gerekiyor. CME Group ve Silicon Data'nın açıkladığı hedef piyasaya sürüm tarihi 2026'nın 5 Ekim'i.
